content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors proposed a straightforward vision transformer-based approach for multivariate irregularly sampled time series classification by converting such time series data into collection of line graphs. The simplicity contrasts with the state-of-the-art performance it has achieved.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
The approach is quite straight forward, and can be potentially extended as a general-purpose method to deal with other kinds of time series analysis tasks.
The experiments were conducted extensively.

Weaknesses
- It is not clearly tested whether “Irregularly Sampled” matters or not. The authors tested the Leaving-sensors-out setting where the observations of a subset of variables are masked. However, the impact of “Irregularly Sampled” was not tested by experimentally generated datasets in which certain amount of data points are dropped from regularly sampled data.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The quality, clarity and originality of this work are sufficient.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors proposed a vision transformer-based approach, named ViTTs, for multivariate irregularly sampled time series classification by converting such time series data into collection of line graphs. It has a potential to extend towards a general-purpose method to deal with other kinds of time series analysis tasks. If the authors emphasize superiority to irregularly sampled data, the method must be tested with several different irregularity.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces vitt (vision transformers) for irregularly sampled time series.  Given D irregularly sampled time series, this paper proposes to convert the time series to independent line graphs and stack these line graphs together (a preprocessing step) and apply a vit model for classification on top of these images with line graphs.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- The paper discusses an important problem in the literature.
- The datasets and results are the same as the study in [1]. This is fine but as the results for example table 3 and table 4 take 1 page (all of which is already in [1]), the current work could spend more time discussing the current work.
- Several assertions in the paper and the discussion need to be revisited or could benefit from a clearer explanation.

[1] https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Kwm8I7dU-l5
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The work and the discussion around the work could be explained better. 
For example, at a first pass the novelty of the work appears to be a preprocessing step which is not new but newly applied to (swin) vits.
content.summary_of_the_review:
- The paper discusses an important problem in the literature.
- Several assertions in the paper need to be revisited or could benefit from a clear explanation. 

Questions:
- In section 3, the work states that the goal is to learn a a function f decomposed in f1 and f2, but Fig 3 representing f1 suggests that f1 is not learned only f2 correct?
- In section 3.1 “we use markers to distinguish observations from the interpolated dots in the line? What does this mean? Interpolation is not shown in fig 1 or discussed subsequently. 
- The authors note that all the methods were trained for 20 epochs. Did they all converge in 20 epochs? 
- Here are we calling vitt the f1 transformation, so is the difference between transformer and vitt the f1 transformation alone? 
- Are the temporal positional embeddings different from the standard positional embeddings in vit? I ask this because in section 3.2 the authors note that they introduce 2 types of embeddings but in table 3 the authors show the results for an ablation study wo positional embeddings.
- The discussion could use some work. For example, the results are shown for 3 datasets but the authors do not  discuss how the number of variables or the length of individual sequences affect the performance of the proposed approach. 
- Furthermore, the authors add at the end of section 4.3 “this might be because square images are more similar to the natural images..” Can the authors clarify this?
- Can the authors provide other evaluating the datasets the authors used?  For example there are no citations for the datasets and metrics section in 4.1, but even citing [1] would make the work clearer. 

[1] https://openreview.net/pdf?id=Kwm8I7dU-l5

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The author has discussed irregular sampled time series in the medical domain application. To address the issue, the author has proposed a  simple and effective approach that convert irregular sampled time series into line graph image. Finally, the author performed an image classification task using the transformer model. Finally, the author has evaluated the proposed approach several
popular healthcare and human activity datasets and claimed outperformed compared to other SOTA algorithms.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

The main reason to accept this paper is empirical results and showing performance o various datasets.

The author has provided more quantitative results on various datasets.


Weaknesses:

The current literature survey does not discuss the advantage and disadvantages of the paper. The author should validate why you should include this paper in this current work.

The problem state is not clear; rather, it's confusing what task will be solved by the author. The author should describe the problem statement and the proposed solution more clearly and in concert.


The author should be an ablation analysis on image formation like if the number of variables is five or more, how will you form the Image? Are you padding or rearranging them? These answers should be discussed in the paper.

The main contribution seems to be position embedding. The author should provide a clear visual picture that describes the proposed local and global positional embedding.

The author mention that the original ViT transformer model doesn't perform well. The final time-series performance is due to the excellent transformer model, or this is due to the core contribution of the paper. This needs to clarify and analyzed more precisely. 


Please provide a sample time series with more than four variables, grid layout, and final image size. Please provide samples of PAM dataset set, which seems to be more generic concerning image size and grid layout since the image size is much different in PAM dataset. How did you rearrange and pass through the transformer model? It would be more interesting to know about various artifacts of the Image, like converting 256 x 320 to standard image size (224 x 224 or 384 x 384) for ViT or SWIN transformer, since it is a synthetic image with different variables. What are the issues you faced when processing the Image, and how did you solve them?  


The author has missed an ablation analysis on the temporal positional embedding.


Technical innovation in this paper is limited, and the design is still incremental.

The given time series sample has four variables. How will it adjust for the odd number of variables? How will you relate patch size, number of variables, and image size?  
 
 
 You have used the Swin transformer, which is a state-of-the-art method.
 It uses a patch size is 4x4; if the number of the variable in the time series increases to 5 or 6, how will you construct an image? It would be more interesting to know the local position embedding and global position embedding in this case and also to know more about inter and intra-communication in the image space.
 
 
 Image preserves local neighborhood property. Each pixel and its neighborhood pixel have a similar property when an  Image is constructed using four or more variable images; the boundary of each sub-image is discontinuity behavior. This crease a blocking artifact in the Image. 
 

-However, I feel that the paper misses one of the core aspects of machine learning practice: readability and reproducibility of results. For instance, the inference details are missing. What is the size of the networks and the components in the proposed method? The author should provide an algorithm or pseudocode to reproduce the results, which this paper misses.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Please refer to the weakness section.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Justification :
The overall writing quality is ok, and the proposed method is simple and beneficial. However, the experiment comparison lacks justification, and the technical contribution is plain.

content.title: Question about Implementation and ablation studies
content.comment: This work is exciting and I want to ask some questions about it.  I tried to implement the model based on the paper and utilize the P12 dataset. However, the difference between my results and the reported results is not negligible. I wonder if the author could provide an anonymous code link to help me figure out the issue.  In addition, the authors ran 5 data splits without reporting the variance for simplicity. However, the ViTT variance in Table 3 is not small. For example,  the AUPRC is "49.4±2.9" in Table 3 and is 48.0 w/o pos. emb in Table 5 on P12. It seems like the difference is in 1 standard deviation, which is not significant. (The same finding is found in P19).  The same question exists in Table 6, in which the authors reported the variance. It seems like the result between different resolutions is not significant.
